#93707. Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.
  • In a recent development, the organization’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta.
  • “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Massive Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers.

In a recent development, the organization’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.”.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.

Meta’s statement about re-evaluating its 2030 emissions goal is a significant public acknowledgment, given that Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have all stuck by their original sustainability goals so far.

But all the companies have acknowledged challenges in balancing their original sustainability goals against the breakneck buildout of hyperscale data centers. Despite efforts to invest in more renewable energy projects, Meta and its rivals are still often pushing forward on AI data centers that rely on burning natural gas to generate electricity.

Meta’s report described the manufacturer’s total emissions as surging from 15.6 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025.

It has been revealed that that would make Meta’s annual carbon footprint roughly comparable to total emissions for the state of Idaho, while surpassing the total emissions of states such as Hawaii, Maine, South Dakota, and Latest Hampshire. The firm attributed much of this emissions increase to “capital goods,” like as data center servers.

That also represents a nearly 40 percent increase in Meta’s carbon footprint between 2024 and 2025, which is the highest percentage year-over-year increase for total emissions reported by any of the four major US tech giants.

In a recent development, for comparison, Microsoft reported a 25 percent increase in its overall carbon footprint, Google reported an 18 percent increase, and Amazon’s report described a 16 percent increase between 2024 and 2025. However, Meta still likely has one of the smallest total carbon footprints among the Major Tech companies.

Meta’s approach to achieving net-zero emissions has included developing latest renewable energy projects to match emissions and using carbon removal technology.

But even when factoring in such efforts, Meta still reported net emissions increasing from more than 8.1 million metric tonnes to more than 11.8 million metric tonnes for 2025. That represents a 45 percent increase.

From a water consumption standpoint, Meta reported progress in reducing facility consumption from 825 million gallons in 2024 to 790 million gallons in 2025.

Yet that positive trend is tempered by the fact that Meta also described an increase in water consumption from “areas with water stress,” rising from 198 million gallons in 2024 to 246 million gallons in 2025.

Industry observers note that meta also reported a sharp increase in water consumption related to purchased electricity—the amount of water consumed by related power generation—from 19 billion gallons in 2024 to more than 26 billion gallons in 2025. This once again highlights that, for data centers, the far bigger water usage comes from the power plants that supply electricity to data centers as opposed to data centers directly using water for cooling.

Still, some minor credit is due. The publication Data Center Dynamics pointed out that “Meta is the only hyperscaler to report indirect water use, a growing concern as data centers shift to closed-loop cooling systems that, despite using less water at source, require more electricity to run.”.

It would very much be in the public interest for other Big Tech companies to follow suit on the reporting front—and public pressure continues to build after the AI backlash impact on US midterm election results.

'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz?
  • For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar-winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich.
  • Recent findings suggest that the same goes for all other famous actors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz? When you're in a German cinema.

For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar-winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich.

Recent findings suggest that the same goes for all other famous actors. In Germany's €125-million ($138-million) voiceover industry, Hollywood's up-and-comers are "adopted" by a voice actor who provides their German voice — often for decades — ensuring continuity and a certain relationship to the stars for audiences.

But on Netflix, and perhaps elsewhere, many of those voices might be about to change.

Recently, Fröhlich and fellow voice actors Anne Helm (Margot Robbie) and Luise Helm (Scarlett Johansson) published a video on social media, letting their followers know they wouldn't provide their voices anymore.

The reason? They refuse to sign Netflix's contract, seen by DW, which contains a clause that lets the American entertainment giant use their voices for training its AI.

Industry observers note that they're not the first voiceover artists to speak out on the topic. But they are the first ones to go viral.

"It was unexpected, completely," Fröhlich said. "For whatever reason, we managed to reach people, perhaps because … we are three well-known women in the voiceover industry.".

"Over the years, we've managed to make good names for ourselves. It seems to have touched people that we made this statement together," she said.

In a recent development, the fresh AI clause has been in Netflix's contracts since January 2026. Voice actors sign one ahead of every production. It was negotiated by BFFS, Germany's union for film and television actors.

Industry observers note that fröhlich, like a significant number of voice actors, is not a member and feels as though the union went over their heads. However, BFFS says the deal gives them protection they wouldn't otherwise have.

Till Völger, an attorney and member of the union's board, states previous contracts and those with other streaming services are silent on AI or contain sweeping AI permissions.

If an AI-generated voice doesn't sound like a particular person, companies are free to use the data they have gathered as they wish. Training can take place in other jurisdictions and may not require the actor's consent at all, he pointed out.

"We have a massive, massive protection gap," Völger told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, against that backdrop, BFFS argues the deal with Netflix is a step forward. It allows the organization to train its own systems with recordings, but voice actors must give separate, explicit consent before their recordings are used to create actual AI-generated voices, even if the voice isn't recognizable as theirs.

"We've created a contractual right that the law doesn't provide," said Völger. "Is the situation perfect? No. Is it better than before? Yes.".

According to recent reports, he would like to see other streaming services agree to the same conditions that Netflix has. In his view, only legislation could create the necessary protections voice actors are seeking.

Netflix says human performance "is and remains crucial to us," in statement provided to DW.

"In recent years, we have commissioned thousands of hours of German dubbing, and we intend to continue supporting a similar volume of work and the use of human voices," the statement continued.

Matti Klemm, the voice of Jason Momoa and beloved children's cartoon elephant Benjamin Blümchen, sees things differently. Like Fröhlich, he is refusing to sign the newly introduced contract.

"In short, it notes: as soon as I record something for Netflix, I'm automatically training their AI, for free," he told DW. "My job is to create a German original, a dubbed version with my performance, not to train the computer systems of some tech companies.".

He is taking Netflix to court, backed by the Society for Civil Rights (GFF), to find out how his voice has been used for training in previous projects.

According to Davy Wang, who is coordinating the case for Klemm and GFF, the lawsuit will seek to stop Netflix using his recordings for training, disclose how previous data was used and establish whether Klemm is entitled to any damages.

It has been revealed that the suit will be filed at the end of the year or in early 2027. Supporters donated more than €50,000 to the legal fund in the first week following its announcement.

For Klemm, what is at stake goes beyond training. "It's not about our voice, it's about our soul, our performance, the way we are," he noted. "How far have we come when AI training matters more than my actual work?".

Netflix remarked it cannot comment on a case that has not yet been filed.

According to recent reports, for a multimillion-euro industry, the outcome of the case could reach well beyond Netflix and other companies and creative branches are watching. But no matter what the outcome of the lawsuit or contract agreements, voice actors' fears for their future run deep.

Those who don't sign contracts can't work, and streaming companies can make up a significant part of their income.

Sources indicate that "Many say: I've held out for 10 months, but I can't anymore. I have to sign this contract, I have to pay my rent, I have to feed my children," explained Fröhlich.

Beyond that, many fear the future of their industry and the connections they have formed with stars and audiences.

"For a many people I'm connected with Cameron Diaz and I evoke something within them," stated Fröhlich.

In a recent development, but if Diaz is involved in more Netflix projects, "then I've basically lost her," she concluded. "I'll never be her voice again.".

Ex-GM CEO on Mary Barra succession planning: 'It's going to be tough'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".
  • The 78-year-old businessman and U.S.
  • Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".

He should know. The 78-year-old businessman and U.S. Navy veteran helped with his own succession planning and recommended to GM's board in 2013 that Barra replace him as CEO. She has held the top job since Jan. 15, 2014.

Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.

In a recent development, "It's going to be very, very dynamic," Akerson told CNBC during a phone interview. "It's going to be a big change.".

Akerson declined to discuss potential internal candidates such as GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, CFO Paul Jacobson or President Mark Reuss, but he remarked the eventual successor needs to be dynamic and, if from the outside, "adaptable.".

Sources indicate that his comments to CNBC follow a Wall Street Journal report on Tuesday that GM is working with an executive search firm to identify possible outside candidates to succeed Barra, in addition to internal prospects. GM declined to comment on the report or Barra's succession.

Akerson, who came to GM as an outsider from The Carlyle Group in 2010, stated selecting an outside candidate might be risky if there are already executives within the organization who have similar leadership and technical expertise.

It has been revealed that "Is there anybody in the organization that has that background that you know better day to day over a period of time? You may be taking a risk by bringing in an outsider," he noted.

The prospect of an outsider leading GM would be unusual in the auto industry, where major automakers have generally promoted internal CEO candidates, apart from periods of exceptional disruption such as the Great Recession.

Stellantis, BMW, Toyota Motor, Nissan Motor and Hyundai Motor have all appointed internal executives to their CEO positions in recent years.

Barra has stated several times that her successor and her longevity in the role would be determined by the board.

A notable influence is likely Hewlett Packard veteran Patricia Russo, GM's longest-serving board member who has been on the board since 2009 and leads its CEO succession planning as independent lead director.

Industry observers note that GM's CEO succession planning is done "at least annually," according to the manufacturer's yearly proxy filing. That process includes Barra providing the board "with recommendations for, and evaluations of, potential CEO successors and discusses developmental intends for these successors," according to the filing.

That is followed by board members engaging "with CEO candidates and senior management talent at Board and committee meetings and other forums to enable directors to personally assess candidates.".

When Akerson was preparing to retire, Barra was among a pool of four candidates — two longtime GM employees and two relative newcomers — who were finalists for CEO in 2013, he said.

Akerson said he put the finalists through an extended evaluation, asking how they viewed GM's strengths and weaknesses, how they would organize the company, and their willingness to work together, potentially with other CEO candidates who didn't get the job.

Sources indicate that akerson stated the final decision to appoint Barra was done at a day-and-a-half-long board meeting in Washington. The candidate field was narrowed to Barra and former GM executive Dan Ammann, an ex-Wall Street banker who was GM's CFO before leaving the automaker's Cruise unit, reportedly over a disagreement in strategy with Barra, in 2021.

It has been revealed that "Mary's very deserving of all the accolades she's received," Akerson said. "She's done a terrific job.".

Barra has been leading the automaker for nearly 13 years, which makes her the longest-serving CEO of the automaker since Alfred Sloan retired after a 23-year career as CEO in 1946.

Akerson said he believes that, like he did, Barra will have major influence in picking her successor. He described that dynamic as integral to continuing her legacy leading the automaker.

According to recent reports, "This is crucial. I think if she doesn't pick the right person, in four or five years from now and things are back in the trough, that will tarnish her history. But I think she'll pick the right one," he said.

#93694. A Former DOGE Operative Won a Federal Contract. Then Things Got Messy

A Former DOGE Operative Won a Federal Contract. Then Things Got Messy

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yet another former member of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) appears to have exited the government only to return as a contractor.
  • In September, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) put out a call for a contract worth $200,000 for “modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement.” Four days later, the department closed the bidding process and awarded the contract to Yat Choi LLC, a organization owned by a former Airbnb engineer and Canadian citizen named Yat Choi, whose company also goes by the name GovMaxxing.
  • Sources indicate that at the time, Choi had left his role at the National Design Studio (NDS)—the group tasked with redesigning government websites—just a few weeks prior.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yet another former member of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) appears to have exited the government only to return as a contractor.

In September, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) put out a call for a contract worth $200,000 for “modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement.” Four days later, the department closed the bidding process and awarded the contract to Yat Choi LLC, a organization owned by a former Airbnb engineer and Canadian citizen named Yat Choi, whose company also goes by the name GovMaxxing.

Sources indicate that at the time, Choi had left his role at the National Design Studio (NDS)—the group tasked with redesigning government websites—just a few weeks prior. Before that, Choi worked at DOGE.

The bid was for a project set to run for a little under six months, and the contract was awarded as sole-source, meaning that it did not go through a normal competitive bidding process. In the documentation announcing the award, HHS justified this decision by saying that its “market research and source rationale found that conventional consulting firms generally would need to assemble a multidisciplinary team or obtain additional technical resources” to provide the required skills around “business-process modernization, artificial intelligence, automation, technical architecture, and rapid prototyping.”.

In October, a organization called CoA Solutions lodged what’s known as a bid protest with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) contesting the agency’s decision to award the contract to Choi. CoA Solutions is a small business that builds AI software for the government and received another contract with the Treasury Department in 2024.

Ari Perez, the CEO of CoA Solutions, tells WIRED that his organization made a bid below the $200,000 award price, and it proposed two experts doing the work full-time, including Perez himself.

Recent findings suggest that perez says that CoA asked HHS for an explanation of the award on October 8 and, when it did not receive one, filed its protest with the GAO the next day. Perez says that his company’s sole contestation was about how the bids were evaluated by HHS, not about Choi or his work with NDS.

Sources indicate that “I'm a service-disabled veteran. I've served this government since I was 17 at West Point. At the US Digital Service I helped deliver for veterans at the VA, and later I worked on asylum and immigration systems at DHS. I started CoA to keep doing impactful government work,” says Perez. “We want to win on merit, and if HHS reopens it, we'll bid again.”.

In a recent development, according to CoA, in response to the bid protest, HHS terminated the award to Choi and canceled the call for contractors. With the cancellation, the GAO dismissed the protest without investigating it further. A GAO spokesperson referred WIRED to HHS.

“HHS remains committed to modernizing its systems to improve efficiency and better serve the American people,” states HHS spokesperson Grace Davis Jamison. “Following a bid protest challenging the award, HHS voluntarily took corrective action, terminating the contract at no cost to the government and canceling the solicitation.”.

According to recent reports, choi’s role in the US government has not been exactly clear. In his bio on X, Choi writes that he was part of both DOGE and NDS, and mentioned in a post that he was recruited by billionaire Elon Musk and Joe Gebbia, Airbnb’s cofounder, to help modernize the retirement system at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM). Gebbia now leads NDS, which was created after Musk left government and which has served as a landing pad for several DOGE members, including Edward “Substantial Balls” Coristine.

It has been revealed that in December 2025, Choi contributed to a blog on the NDS website about automating the federal retirement system. But on his LinkedIn, Choi lists himself as a senior technologist at OPM. On November 5, just two days after Republicans lost the midterm elections, Choi unveiled in a post on X that he had left OPM and was launching his company, GovMaxxing, through which he plans to continue to contract with the government. GovMaxxing operates as Yat Choi LLC federally.

It has been revealed that in response to questions from WIRED about his role in government, Choi says that he “was recruited to support federal modernization efforts and subsequently onboarded as an OPM contractor.” There, Choi says, he “contributed to modernization efforts associated with DOGE and subsequently NDS. I was not, and have never been, a federal government employee.” Choi claims he left OPM in mid-August, though OPM did not respond to questions confirming whether this was the case. “I began actively pursuing the contracting opportunity after my engagement with OPM ended,” says Choi.

It has been revealed that choi confirmed that he is a Canadian citizen and a “lawful permanent resident” of the US. Foreigners are not generally allowed to hold full-time roles in government or serve as special government employees. The rules are more flexible for contractors. During the height of DOGE’s activity, a close Musk ally, Baris Akis, was prevented from joining the group as a special government employee because he is a Turkish citizen, according to The Atlantic. Akis, however, continued to serve as a recruiter for the group.

On his website, Choi labels the “client” for his work in government as “US Office of Personnel Management / DOGE / National Design Studio” and describes himself as the “modernization lead.” However, documents indicate that Choi’s company was not registered in the state of Latest York until April 2026, and in the System for Award Management, the procurement website where US government contractors bid, there are no other contracts for Choi’s work. “None of my work at OPM was performed through my LLC. My website references my prior professional experience at OPM and does not attribute that work to my company,” states Choi.

Recent findings suggest that choi claims that the HHS contract was for a “separate modernization discovery project. It was not a continuation of any work with OPM, DOGE, or NDS.”.

According to the code of federal regulations, except in very specific circumstances, government contracts cannot be awarded to government employees or to organizations they fully or partially own. But Jessica Tillipman, associate dean for government procurement law studies at George Washington University, says that even though Choi was not a regular government employee, the fact that he was part of DOGE and NDS, whose work has spanned across government agencies, could create the appearance of a conflict of interest with regard to the HHS contract. “The baseline posture of the federal acquisition regulation is to strictly avoid conflicts of interest or even the appearance of them,” says Tillipman. “So agencies all have a duty, and the contracting teams have a duty, to make sure that they are considering these things when they're awarding these contracts.”.

Sources indicate that choi tells WIRED that HHS “initiated contact and expressed interest” in his “modernization experience” before the call for bids was confirmed. HHS did not respond to questions about whether the bid had been written specifically for him.

According to recent reports, tillipman notes that while the government may sometimes create a contracting opportunity designed for a specific person or tech giant, “it’s generally niche or highly specialized work." Tillipman notes that the fact that there were 75 bids placed on the contract indicates that this is “not a unique service.” She notes that the government’s justification for a sole-source contract is “thin.” “Usually, when there's only one responsible source, there's a technical reason,” she says. This could be something like a special tool that is not interoperable with outside software, or when there is only one company that can provide a specific service or that makes a certain physical part that might be used for weapons or specialized machinery.

On the GovMaxxing website, Choi notes that potential government clients can work with the manufacturer as a prime contractor or “subcontract through one of our partner primes your agency may already be working with.” Unlike prime contracts, there is no way to publicly see which subcontractor a prime contractor works with. Choi declined to name the companies or current “prime” contractors he subcontracts under.

But Tillipman states that even if Choi were to take on another version of the HHS contract for a subcontractor, similar questions could still be raised within the agency and externally should it ever come to light. “In certain instances, your subcontractors’ conflicts can be imputed to the prime contractor,” she says. “The whole thing is highly irregular overall.”.

Choi is not the only former DOGE or NDS member who appears to be hoping to benefit from federal contracts after leaving the government. Earlier this year, WIRED reported that Ethan Shaotran, one of the young engineers who formed the early core of DOGE, had started a defense tech startup. The startup has been listed on the System for Award Management since April. Former DOGE members Jack Stein, Gavin Kliger, Luke Farritor, and Marko Elez launched an AI defense technology tech giant called Cathedral, which has been listed on the System for Award Management since July. Neither have received “prime” contracts with any federal agency, but whether they have been taken on as subcontractors to other prime contractors is unclear.

It has been revealed that despite the HHS contract’s cancellation, Choi appears undeterred. Earlier this week, following the nationwide grounding of flights by the Federal Aviation Administration, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called for funding to modernize air traffic control in a post on X. In response, Choi wrote, “Secretary Duffy, I’m the DOGE engineer who led the modernization of federal retirement processing at OPM last year … I’ve since started a organization to work with more agencies, and we’d love to help with the FAA’s modernization efforts. Put us in, coach!”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed.
  • Sources indicate that google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the fresh desktop search page after a successful test.
  • The search button has obviously been a part of Google’s search page forever.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that has been in testing for the past few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely.

Sources indicate that google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the fresh desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There’s an image-generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The “I’m Feeling Lucky” button remains, but the Google Search button that sat next to it is gone.

The search button has obviously been a part of Google’s search page forever. However, it wasn’t in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search.

The other substantial change brings your recent AI conversations to the forefront. If you’re logged in to Google, the search homepage will have an expandable sidebar on the left with your recent AI Mode search threads. This sidebar will also be accessible on the results page. According to Stein, the sidebar made a “big difference” in how people made progress on their web searches, calling it a “simpler way to pick up where you left off.”.

Industry observers note that it’s easy to feel frustrated by changes like this if you don’t like Google’s fresh AI approach to search. But at the same time, the loss of functionality is minimal. Google probably has usage data that indicates that particular search button was rarely used. Most people probably just hit Enter or click an autocomplete suggestion to go to the results.

This change says more about Google’s priorities and the future of search. AI features get prominent buttons, and your AI conversations now have a whole sidebar UI. Meanwhile, traditional search is increasingly de-emphasized. There may come a day when AI Mode takes over completely, forcing you to manually select the old-fashioned version of search. It does feel like Google is inching in that direction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple's most affordable and most vibrant laptop has only been out since this past March, but it sounds like the organization will offer a spiffy newly introduced upgrade sooner rather than later. That's hardly a surprise, given the success of the product so far.

That's what Mark Gurman of Bloomberg is reporting, anyway. In his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman predicted that Apple will sell a second iteration of the MacBook Neo most likely by the end of March 2027. That timing is meant to line up with the iOS/macOS 27.4 upgrade cycle, at which point Gurman indicates we could also see the iPhone 18 and 18e models, a new OLED iPad Air, and a new budget iPad.

According to recent reports, apple upgrading a laptop just a year after release is not unheard of. In recent years, the manufacturer has been releasing annual upgrades of its MacBook Air and Pro lines, outfitting the devices with the latest Apple Silicon, sometimes with few other changes.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

As for what to expect from the fresh MacBook Neo, it doesn't sound like a hugely substantial upgrade at this point in time. From a usability standpoint, the most crucial thing Gurman mentioned is that the A18 Pro chip powering the original Neo will be upgraded to an A19 chip, with RAM bumped from 8GB to 12GB as well.

It remains to be seen if the current $699 starting price for the MacBook Neo will go up, but it's definitely a possibility. We do live in a RAMageddon world, after all, and Apple has already raised the price of the Neo once. It's also worth pointing out that the A19 chip powering the Neo 2 would still be less capable than the M-series chips powering more expensive Mac computers. Even the fresh iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have an A20 Pro chip.

In a recent development, beyond the chip improvement, Apple is also looking to add fresh MacBook Neo colors "frequently," per Gurman. However, Gurman didn't say for certain whether or not that will start with the second iteration of the budget laptop. The first version came in silver, indigo, blush, and citrus, so Apple definitely has room to add even more hues for people to enjoy.

According to recent reports, alex Perry is a tech reporter at Mashable who primarily covers video games and consumer tech. Alex has spent most of the last decade reviewing games, smartphones, headphones, and laptops, and he doesn’t proposal on stopping anytime soon. Finland's Prime Minister Sanna Marin concedes election

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.
  • The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data highlighted with all ballots counted.
  • “We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo stated in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finland’s left-wing Prime Minister Sanna Marin conceded defeat on Sunday in the Nordic country’s parliamentary election as the opposition right-wing National Coalition Party (NCP) claimed victory in a tightly fought contest.

The pro-business NCP was expected to win 48 of the 200 seats in parliament, narrowly ahead of the nationalist Finns Party with 46 seats and Marin’s Social Democrats on 43 seats, justice ministry election data highlighted with all ballots counted.

“We got the biggest mandate,” NCP leader Petteri Orpo stated in a speech to followers, vowing to “fix Finland” and its economy.

He will get the first chance at forming a coalition to obtain majority in parliament as Marin’s era as prime minister was expected to end.

Popular abroad, at home Marin faces battle to keep her job.

“We have gained support, we have gained more seats (in parliament). That’s an excellent achievement, even if we did not finish first today,” the prime minister noted in a speech to party members.

Marin, 37, the world’s youngest prime minister when she took office in 2019, is considered by fans around the globe as a millennial role model for progressive upcoming leaders, but at home she has faced criticism for her partying and her government’s public spending.

Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin takes drug test following partying backlash.

While she remains very popular among many Finns, particularly young moderates, she antagonized some conservatives with lavish spending on pensions and education they see as not frugal enough.

The NCP has led in polls for almost two years although its lead had melted away in recent months. It has promised to curb spending and stop the rise of public debt, which has reached just over 70% of GDP since Marin took office in 2019.

Orpo accused Marin of eroding Finland’s economic resilience at a time when Europe’s energy crisis, driven by Russia’s war in Ukraine, has hit the country hard and the cost of living has increased.

Orpo has noted he will negotiate with all groups to obtain a majority in parliament, while Marin has said her Social Democrats may govern with the NCP but will not go into government with the Finns Party.

Marin called the Finns Party “openly racist” during a debate in January – an accusation the nationalist group rejected.

The Finns Party’s main goal is to reduce what leader Riikka Purra has called “harmful” immigration from developing countries outside the European Union. It also calls for austerity policies to curb deficit spending, a stance it shares with the NCP.

Most notable of Marin’s foreign policy actions has been her push, along with President Sauli Niinisto, for the country to make a watershed policy U-turn by seeking NATO membership in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

That process is now almost complete, with Helsinki expected to join within days after all the Western defense alliance’s 30 members approved the accession.

#93685. RIIZE brought their online fandom into the real world. I was there to see it.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1857 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

RIIZE brought their online fandom into the real world. I was there to see it.

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that that was one of my first thoughts on Friday night as I watched K-pop group RIIZE perform for roughly 600 fans at Brooklyn Steel in Latest York City.
  • It's a funny contradiction, considering the entire premise of the evening was to bring digital fandom into the physical world.
  • The occasion was Spotify CLOSER, a fresh live music series that brings artists and their most dedicated listeners together for intimate performances and conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We need to bring back MTV Unplugged.

Recent findings suggest that that was one of my first thoughts on Friday night as I watched K-pop group RIIZE perform for roughly 600 fans at Brooklyn Steel in Latest York City. There were no elaborate stage productions or arena-sized crowds. Instead, there were stripped-down performances, candid conversations, a few wonderfully awkward moments, and a sea of smartphones held high above the audience.

Seriously, everyone had their phones out.

It's a funny contradiction, considering the entire premise of the evening was to bring digital fandom into the physical world. But maybe that's just what being a fan looks like in 2026. Even when we're standing a few feet away from our favorite artists, we still want to capture the moment, preserve it, and inevitably share it with everyone who couldn't be there.

The occasion was Spotify CLOSER, a fresh live music series that brings artists and their most dedicated listeners together for intimate performances and conversations. After launching in Seoul in Oct., the series made its U.S. debut on Nov. 20 with RIIZE, bringing together more than 600 fans from the New York tri-state area, many of whom were identified as the group's top local listeners and selected based on their listening habits.

In a recent development, since debuting under SM Entertainment in 2023, RIIZE — consisting of Shotaro, Eunseok, Sungchan, Wonbin, Sohee, and Anton — has emerged as one of K-pop's most prominent fifth-generation acts, performing at major festivals like Austin City Limits and Lollapalooza South America. But despite their growing international popularity, the group has only toured the U.S. once, making opportunities for American fans to see them in person relatively rare.

For many, their relationship with RIIZE has largely unfolded online, through music, livestreams, social media, and the seemingly endless stream of content that makes K-pop fandom feel like a full-time commitment.

In other words, the same platform that connected these fans to RIIZE's music was now bringing them face-to-face with the six people behind it. And I was curious to see what would happen when that connection moved offline.

Before RIIZE even took the stage, Spotify had transformed Brooklyn Steel into something of a playground for BRIIZE, the group's devoted fandom.

There was a fisheye photo station, branded Spotify x RIIZE microphone keychains, and an area where fans could write letters to the members. Nearby, six lockers offered a glimpse into each member's personality, decorated with objects representing their individual interests.

Recent findings suggest that shotaro's locker featured a camera and bucket hat, while Eunseok's included boxing gloves and a Doraemon plushie. Sungchan's was outfitted with a soccer ball and cleats, and Wonbin's displayed Nike Air Force 1s and earbuds. Sohee's locker featured a Boston cap and Naruto figures, while Anton's contained a violin and swimming goggles. Each member had also written a personal letter to BRIIZE.

For longtime fans, these weren't just random objects. They were familiar details, the kinds of things you pick up from watching livestreams and behind-the-scenes content. You can know an idol's favorite foods, recognize their sense of humor, and feel familiar with their friendships without ever having met them. Seeing these details arranged in physical space felt a little like stepping inside the digital world fans had spent years getting to know.

According to recent reports, and that was the interesting thing about the event. Spotify wasn't simply bringing fans closer to RIIZE by putting them in a smaller room. It was recreating the familiarity of online fandom in a setting where fans could participate, leaving their own messages alongside the members' handwritten notes.

Of course, once RIIZE appeared, nearly every phone in the room went up, mine included. So much for going offline.

According to recent reports, the crowd was enthusiastic and eager to interact, with handwritten signs scattered throughout the audience. My personal favorite was a sign directed at Anton that simply read, "Slap me." (I have questions, but I respect the commitment.).

Recent findings suggest that anton, who grew up in Latest Jersey, received particularly enthusiastic cheers from the Garden State contingent. There was also a very crucial geography lesson in which fans informed the members that Peter Parker, aka Spider-Man, is from New York. You know, the essential cultural exchange that happens when a K-pop group visits the city.

These were the kinds of interactions that made the evening feel less like a conventional concert and more like a gathering of people who already knew one another, even if most of them had never actually met.

And for RIIZE, it was an opportunity to put faces to the streaming numbers.

RIIZE opened the night with "Get A Guitar," their 2023 debut single, performed entirely in English for the first time. The setlist also included "Boom Boom Bass," "Impossible," "D-D-Done," "Love 119," and the first U.S. performance of "Do your dance.".

But the evening wasn't just about the music. Between performances, the members participated in a Q&A hosted by Anton, who served as the group's unofficial emcee and occasional English translator. He kept the conversation moving, prompting his bandmates to answer questions and helping bridge the language gap with the predominantly English-speaking audience, while live subtitles appeared on the screens.

Initially, the members seemed a little reserved. Away from the familiar structure of a performance or the carefully edited chaos of variety content, there was a certain shyness to their early exchanges, as though they were still finding their footing in a more spontaneous setting.

According to recent reports, but as the Q&A progressed, that initial hesitation gave way to something more playful. The members began teasing one another, laughing more freely, and engaging with the crowd. Sohee, in particular, seemed to come alive as the night went on. Funny, expressive, and naturally charismatic, he grew increasingly comfortable commanding the room, revealing a different side of the confidence he already brings to the stage as one of the group's standout vocalists.

It was fun to watch that transformation happen in real-time.

Industry observers note that during one segment, the members voted on which of them best fit a series of superlatives. Sungchan was named the funniest, Anton earned the title of biggest flirt, and Shotaro received a unanimous vote for best smile. The conversations were sometimes silly, occasionally awkward, and all the more charming for it.

In a recent development, my favorite exchange came when Shotaro was expressing his appreciation for the fans. After delivering a heartfelt message, he earnestly added, "Please forget that.".

Anton was quick to correct him: "Please don't forget that.".

In a recent development, that small moment captured the easygoing charm of the night. RIIZE are a group accustomed to the precision of rehearsed performances, but here, in front of hundreds of fans, they were navigating something far less predictable. There was no choreography to fall back on, no script for a misplaced word or an unexpected laugh. Just six guys figuring it out together, and letting their personalities shine in the process.

For all the playful banter and fan interactions, the moment that stayed with me most was RIIZE's performance of their upcoming single, "Insomnia.".

The song is already one of the group's more understated offerings, performed without choreography, but for Spotify CLOSER, RIIZE took that intimacy a step further with a new, even more stripped-down arrangement. The performance put the focus squarely on their voices, allowing their harmonies to shine and giving the song a different kind of emotional weight. There was something lovely about hearing a song that was already relatively restrained given even more room to breathe.

It was the closest the evening came to the spirit of MTV Unplugged, the iconic music series that invited artists to reinterpret their work in a more intimate setting.

That's not to say RIIZE needed to abandon the choreography or elaborate performances that are so integral to K-pop. But there's something special about hearing artists approach their own material from a different perspective, especially when it brings out details that might otherwise go unnoticed.

Watching "Insomnia," I found myself missing that kind of music programming — the opportunity to see artists experiment with familiar songs, to hear their voices in a fresh context, and to experience a performance that feels entirely specific to a particular room and moment.

Recent findings suggest that spotify CLOSER isn't quite Unplugged, nor does it need to be. But the appeal feels similar. Sometimes, hearing a familiar song in a different way is enough to make you appreciate it all over again.

There's a certain irony in a streaming platform creating an event designed to bring fans away from their screens. Especially when nearly everyone in the room was holding up a phone.

Sources indicate that spotify CLOSER is, of course, a branded experience. It's a way to reward highly engaged listeners while creating exclusive content that can eventually circulate on the platform. Select performances from the evening will be released on Spotify, allowing fans around the world to experience some of what happened in Brooklyn.

In a recent development, but the commercial nature of the event doesn't make the connection any less meaningful. If anything, the night illustrated how intertwined our digital and physical experiences of fandom have become.

It has been revealed that the fans at Brooklyn Steel didn't leave their online identities at the door. They brought their phones, their handwritten signs, their knowledge of the members' personalities, and all the inside jokes and shared references they'd accumulated from following RIIZE online. And the members, who initially seemed a little timid, gradually relaxed into the kind of playful, slightly clumsy interactions fans have come to love through their screens.

As the evening drew to a close, RIIZE expressed their hopes of returning to Upcoming York before ending with an encore performance of "One Kiss.".

For all the ways technology has made artists more accessible than ever, there's still something it can't quite replicate: the spontaneity of sharing a room, where a mistranslated word can become a joke, a fan's sign can spark a conversation, and a familiar song can sound entirely latest.

And for the record, Shotaro, I won't forget that.

Topics Music Fandom K-Pop Spotify.

Her work has appeared in Teen Vogue, Rolling Stone, PAPER, NYLON, ELLE, Glamour, NME, W, The FADER, and elsewhere on the internet.

She's exceptionally fluent in fandom and will gladly make you a K-pop playlist and/or provide anime recommendations upon request. Crystal lives in Upcoming York City with her two black cats, Howl and Sophie.

It has been revealed that parenting is exhausting. If there’s a fresh parent in your life, whether it’s your friend who is the new parent of the group or a family member who just had a baby, there are a lot of ways to show some love. Showing up, checking in on how they're surviving, and bringing something that can improve their life are all great ways to support the new parents in your circle.

It has been revealed that there’s a lot of parenting and baby gear out there, and not all of it is created equal. Not all of it will suit what the parents in your life might need, either. This guide is organized into a handful of categories of parenting gadgets, smart home gear, little luxuries, and even food deliveries you can send to their door. All of these are tried and tested by WIRED’s reviewers, many of whom are parents and can confirm the difference it’s made in their lives.

Looking for more baby gear or gift ideas? Don’t miss our gifts for moms and dads or our guide to all the best baby gear.

Updated November 2026: We've added the Calpak Car Organizer, Solly Baby Wrap, and Tubby Todd's gift sets as upcoming gifts to this guide, and a discount code for CookUnity.

According to recent reports, it’s easy to remember to register for things like the car seat and baby clothes. But there are a lot of small gadgets that make parenting a little easier, things that latest parents don’t realize they might love using. Here are some of the favorites from the parents at WIRED.

Baby nails are sharp, but it’s also easy to clip their tiny nails too far. The solution? An electric nail trimmer. No more scratches on Mom's and Dad's or baby’s upcoming, beautiful faces. Plus it can be less scary for parents than wielding traditional nail clippers near baby’s tiny fingers.

This was a gift from a friend that wasn’t actually on my registry, but I used it more than so many things I did register for. Pacifiers fall all the time and get grimy instantly. I kept this portable UV sterilizer hooked to my diaper bag, and loved popping a pacifier in after drops (after wiping it down with a wet wipe first).

Industry observers note that the Hatch is my most-used item in the last four years. It was easy to set up on the fly when I came home from the hospital, and I love that I can set up a few scenes in the app to flip through depending on whether I was nursing at three a.m. or putting my son to sleep. The Hatch Baby is now in his room and keeps him asleep each night with its music, while I have the Hatch Restore for myself.

According to recent reports, everyone on TikTok might talk about the MomCozy washer, but the best baby bottle washer WIRED reviewer Nicole Kinning found actually comes from Grownsy. It's quiet, has a deep interior cavity to hold tons of bottle and pump parts, and has multiple modes and combinations you can customize for the perfect cleaning session. It circulates HEPA-filtered air to keep bottles sterile after washing.

Early parenting is survival, and bandwidth to go to the grocery store or cook becomes a hard zero. There’s a reason friends and family often run food trains for new parents. The following food gifts would be a great option to contribute to a food train, and being shippable packages means you can send them to a friend or family member you may live too far from to visit often.

Former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage has tried all kinds of prepared meals, and he claims the best one is CookUnity. It’s a ready-to-eat meal delivery service that calls itself a “chef collective”, with regional menus led by regional chefs. Put together a week of meals to send them, or snag them a gift card so they can choose their own. You can also get 50 percent off your first order right now through the end of November with our discount code WIREDCU50.

In a recent development, hook up your favorite new parents with their very own brunch spread. This is a good option to send to their doorstep to feed them for a few days or to bring over in person so they don’t have to worry about having anything prepped. (Great to split with another friend or two for sip and see!) You get to choose up to six bagel flavors, up to three cream cheeses, Nova lox, and can add on more of everything.

I didn’t put anything fun on my firstborn's registry. I was so overwhelmed with how many must-haves I needed (including an infant baby tub device I never used, but every registry site claimed I'd need). Baby registry websites will constantly tell you that you haven’t added things from every single category their site has deemed vital. There are a lot of things parents need, but there are lots of fun things you can gift that aren’t necessities but will still make parenting a little easier, or at least feel like a thoughtful gift.

Shop (The Ultimate Mama + Baby Gift Set).

One of my favorite things to gift at a baby shower or to a newly introduced parent is a nice set of baby-friendly bath and skin-care goods. Sure, a massive bottle of Aveeno will serve them well (it's what you'll usually find in my shower), but this is a fun opportunity to splurge on something nice for them that they will definitely need. I love these sets from Tubby Todd because you have a variety of options to choose from, including just baby or both mom and baby. (Personally, as a pregnant mama, I love the Tubby Todd Belly Oil.).

Sources indicate that this was my dream gift as a first-time mom, and I'm finally getting to use one as a second-timer. I loved wrapping my first with a similar (but cheaper) soft wrap in the early months, but the material on the Solly Baby Wrap is much softer and more breathable. The prints are beautiful, and there's cozier double-knit design options if you live in a colder climate.

It has been revealed that if the new mom or dad in your life is struggling with overstimulation, a nice pair of earplugs could go a long way. The Loop Experience 2 cut down some of the volume and noise without completely blocking out sound. Great for epic meltdowns and colicky days without being unaware of what’s going on. I now just carry mine around on my keychain in case I end up somewhere surprisingly loud or forget to blueprint ahead for a concert.

Where has this organizer been in my four years of parenting? My biggest regret during my son's baby stages was not having a trunk station full of diaper change supplies (and extra clothes). This large car organizer works great for everything from baby gear to keeping your groceries from rolling around and even storing the haphazard amount of toys my son now brings into the car.

My friend gifted me two of these beautiful muslin swaddle blankets, and they were among my most-used items. I used them to swaddle my summer child without worrying he would melt, and I used them for contact naps so I wouldn’t sweat all over him. It was great for a quick car seat cover or a place to sit him down on some grass—the uses are endless, and there’s a ton of gorgeous colors and prints to gift.

Sources indicate that when I had my first child, I fell back into reading to help me stay awake for late-night feeds and contact naps. I read entire series in a matter of days, and I was actually gifted two Kindles for my birthday to help me get off my phone and have a better screen to read on. While my favorite is my Paperwhite, the base Kindle makes for a great gift (and this older version should be on sale soon for Black Friday.).

Industry observers note that I’m biased as a smart home reviewer, but the right Wi-Fi–powered gadget could change your life, especially when you’re locked into a contact nap and need to dim the lights without moving. These are a few smart home upgrades I’d recommend gifting to just about anyone, latest parent or not.

Industry observers note that I love a digital photo frame, especially as a parent. My camera roll has been stuck in a state of constant overflow since my son was born. I love being able to easily upload photos to my Aura frames to enjoy all the time, and as my son has gotten older, he’s loved seeing them too.

These smart light bulbs from Ikea are super cheap and really easy to control and make routines with. Gift them a set with some remote controls that they can put next to the rocking chair, and they can instantly dim or turn off the lights without needing to get up. They’re Matter-compatible and work with Apple HomeKit, too.

This isn’t technically a smart item, but I’m a substantial believer that parents who love tea and hot water need to have a double-walled kettle. It’ll keep little hands from getting burned—and big, sleep-deprived hands that forget how hot a kettle can get.

Mom and Dad deserve painless streaming, but there's no hope for that if the remote gets lost. The Google TV Streamer is a sleek system that can also help you locate the remote with a button on the back of the streamer itself, taking one more task off a tired parent's mind.

You probably already gifted the baby something at the baby shower, but if you want to get something for the little one to play with, here are some of our favorite baby toys as WIRED parents.

A good soft book goes a long way with babies who want to chew on every corner, and I like that some of the corners of this Goodnight Moon soft book are reinforced with a chewable texture.

It has been revealed that A Jellycat is a kid must-have, and there’s no such thing as too many stuffed animals. Jellycat changes its offerings often, so the one you get could become a treasured, irreplaceable stuffie. (Maybe buy a second if the kid gets really attached!).

According to recent reports, I just found my old set of Infantino blocks I had for my son and put them in bags for my second-born-to-be’s toy stash. These large, flexible blocks are easy to stack and safe for baby to stick in their mouths without worrying about choking or sharp corners. This version from Walmart also includes a little activity station to make it easy for your little one to sit and use them.

According to recent reports, lovevery is probably best known for its toy boxes (which are great), but I actually think The Play Gym is one of its best offerings. From months three to seven, this was my kiddo’s absolute favorite place to be. Being in a crowded New York City apartment, having a soft, fun, machine-washable baby space that was easy to move around was invaluable. —Harry Rabinowitz.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking to spend a little more on the new parents, these smart home and connected gadgets will genuinely improve their everyday life. When I tell you that every parent I’ve hooked on a good robot vacuum comes back to me raving about how much it’s helped them—it’s worth the price of entry. If you’re looking for true parenting gear, like the best baby monitors and smart bassinets, I’d check out my guide to the Best Baby Gear instead.

Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.

They mentioned that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.

More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.

Police in Erfurt in Thuringia were among the first to issue a statement on the threats, saying they were responding to threats at "multiple schools" after morning warnings, including in Jena, Erfurt, Mühlhausen, Zella-Mehlis, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt and Greiz.

"The same word-for-word threats were received this morning at the various eductional institutes," police wrote in a press release. "Based on preliminary findings other federal states are also affected by the threatening messages.".

It has been revealed that police said they had no information yet on the potential author or sender of the emails. They were investigating breach of the peace-based crimes via the threat of criminal activity.

"At present the police is not working on the assumption of the bomb threats being serious and recommends that schools do not implement evacuation measures and continue their normal operations," they stated.

Police in Freiburg in the southwest and authorities to the north in Hanover also mentioned they were responding to emailed bomb threats directed against schools.

Similar reports are emerging to the north of Germany in Denmark.

As in Germany, Danish police said they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools.".

This follows other recent cases of coordinated bomb threats against multiple schools that turned out to be hoaxes in Italy earlier in the month.

It also comes amid various apparent bids to create disruption within Europe in recent weeks, such as multiple bomb threats targeting commercial airlines, or hacking into supermarket refrigeration systems to spoil produce en masse.

  • In a recent development, “SpaceX’s potentially unilateral modification of a U.S.
  • CNN first reported the letter’s existence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The representative in the US House expected to chair the House Intelligence Committee in January, Jim Himes (D-Conn.), has threatened to withhold support for funding government-owned systems from SpaceX amid the ongoing inquiry into the use of Starshield in Ukraine.

In a recent development, “SpaceX’s potentially unilateral modification of a U.S. Government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the U.S. Government has with SpaceX,” Himes wrote in a letter to SpaceX founder Elon Musk on Friday.

CNN first reported the letter’s existence. The network also reported that Himes sent a classified communication to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton with a similar message that it would be difficult for Congress to authorize funding for systems with SpaceX as the primary vendor.

SpaceX has developed the consumer Starlink service over the last decade, which provides high-speed Internet from low-Earth orbit to user terminals on Earth. For government customers, SpaceX has also developed Starshield, a suite of satellite services that includes a militarized version of Starlink communications. The US government has purchased Starshield services and extended access to Ukraine, although the terms governing that access are largely classified.

During the last several weeks, a controversy has erupted over interruptions to Starshield service in parts of Ukraine, cutting off connectivity to drones used to defend against Russian attacks.

Industry observers note that on October 19, for example, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said of Starshield on social media, “Unfortunately, we have established that the equipment stops functioning at speeds of 130–161 kilometers per hour in various sectors of the front. This is slowing down our frontline logistics and limiting the use of various types of drones, particularly mid-strike drones and interceptors of jet-powered ‘shaheds.’” Additional disruptions were reported a week ago.

Sources indicate that the central question is who decided to curtail the performance of Starshield assets in Ukraine. Accounts have variously implicated Musk, SpaceX, the Pentagon, and the White House. Musk has noted that US officials control Starshield access, while defending SpaceX’s right to restrict the use of commercial Starlink service in war.

“My ask to you is straightforward,” Himes wrote to Musk. “Explain the changes that were made to the Starshield service in October 2026, why those changes were made, and whether those changes were made unilaterally by SpaceX or were directed by a U.S. Government official.”.

The communications from Himes suggest that congressional Democrats, who will control the House and Senate in January following decisive victories in the midterm elections, are prepared to not just investigate the disruption of these SpaceX services in Ukraine, but to take action that could threaten SpaceX’s broader national security business.

“It is difficult for me to continue supporting the authorization of funding for these SpaceX-developed, government-owned systems, until I receive satisfactory answers to my questions about the Starshield service in Ukraine,” Himes wrote in his letter to Musk.

Various options are open to congressional Democrats, as well as some Republicans who have raised similar concerns, including demanding classified briefings and documents and restricting funding through appropriations to the US Department of Defense and other federal departments. Notably, the US Space Force awarded SpaceX a $2.29 billion contract earlier this year to develop the Space Data Network Backbone intended to support the Golden Dome missile defense initiative. That program, along with SpaceX’s work building intelligence satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office, could become a focus of congressional scrutiny.

It has been revealed that it seems unlikely that the US government would sever ties with SpaceX for space-based data services or introduces, as the company is currently providing capabilities that no other US company can match. But Democrats are clearly serious about putting restrictions on Musk’s ability to influence geopolitical conflicts that have traditionally been the purview of governments rather than corporations.

Britain's pound is beating every other major currency this year

📅 04 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 3 min read (529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the British pound crashed to a record low last fall as investors rebelled against budget aims by former Prime Minister Liz Truss.
  • Sterling hit its highest level against the US dollar in 10 months on Tuesday, topping $1.25 for the first time since June 2022.
  • Industry observers note that the UK currency has been boosted by indications the country’s economy is holding up better than expected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the British pound crashed to a record low last fall as investors rebelled against budget aims by former Prime Minister Liz Truss. Now, it’s enjoying a comeback.

Sterling hit its highest level against the US dollar in 10 months on Tuesday, topping $1.25 for the first time since June 2022. The pound, which has advanced about 3.3% versus the greenback since the start of 2023, is the best-performing currency among developed economies this year.

Industry observers note that the UK currency has been boosted by indications the country’s economy is holding up better than expected. Activity is now thought to have expanded 0.1% in the final three months of last year, up from a previous estimate of no growth at all. Gross domestic product growth in January has been estimated at 0.3% after dropping 0.5% in December.

In a recent development, this resilience is bolstering expectations the Bank of England will maintain aggressive interest rate hikes despite concerns about the health of the global banking sector. Rising rates can boost the domestic currency because they help attract foreign investors searching for higher returns.

Inflation in the United Kingdom also jumped to an annual rate of 10.4% in February, underscoring the need for the Bank of England to maintain its tough approach.

The pound plunged close to $1.03 in September 2022 after the Truss government unveiled aims to boost borrowing while slashing taxes, unleashing panic in financial markets that fueled fears of a recession in the United Kingdom.

The International Monetary Fund predicted in January that the UK economy would contract by 0.6% this year, while all other advanced economies would grow, if only slightly.

“There was a lot of pessimism being priced into the pound,” stated Francesco Pesole, a currency strategist at ING.

But the sharp pullback in energy prices and China’s reopening have provided some relief about the economic outlook since the start of the year.

“There was a big re-rating of growth expectations around Europe, and that impacted the UK,” Pesole said.

Industry observers note that the euro has also been lifted by these dynamics, rising 2.3% against the US dollar in 2023. The pound’s rally has been sharper in large part because its 2022 declines were more severe, according to Pesole.

Both currencies have been aided by the greenback’s sharp drop from highs reached last September as recession fears have percolated in the United States.

A lack of clarity around the Federal Reserve’s next steps has also restrained the dollar in recent weeks. Investor speculation has increased that the Fed could pause or stop rate hikes due to concerns about the economy following the failure of Silicon Valley Bank last month.

According to recent reports, jordan Rochester, a currency strategist at Nomura, mentioned he thinks the pound could rise to $1.30 this year and “potentially higher.” But he still sees risks given the uncertainty surrounding the Bank of England’s prepares and how rate rises will feed back through the country’s economy. And Pesole cautioned that currency fluctuations are often overdone when markets are choppy, as they are now.

“In a volatile market environment, moves are exacerbated,” he said.

If owners make those changes without Tesla, the tech giant can suspend a Cybercab owner's subscription, effectively bricking their car.

In addition, subscriptions can be temporarily suspended without refund if a Cybercab owner operates the vehicle in an improper or unsafe manner.

Recent findings suggest that another rule, at least for now, is that a Cybercab can only be used for personal use. Tesla Cybercabs cannot be used for rentals or with apps like Uber or DoorDash.

Industry observers note that the Tesla Cybercab is also geofenced, meaning it right now can only be used in approved areas of Texas. Attempting to use the car outside of the approved areas can result in operation of the vehicle being "technologically prevented.".

#93663. COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (973 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The longest-running climate talks in history came to a disappointing conclusion on Sunday as negotiators failed to come to an agreement on a shared political direction on climate change.
  • After two days of extended talks, representatives from country after country, tiredness etched into each face, voiced their opposition to the so-called "Antalya Pact.".
  • "I understand that there is no agreement on this text.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The longest-running climate talks in history came to a disappointing conclusion on Sunday as negotiators failed to come to an agreement on a shared political direction on climate change.

After two days of extended talks, representatives from country after country, tiredness etched into each face, voiced their opposition to the so-called "Antalya Pact.".

"I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," mentioned Murat Kurum, Turkish president of the COP31 climate summit.

One of the main sticking points: the words "fossil fuels." While some nations, including petrostates like Saudi Arabia and Russia, wanted them omitted from the text, others saw it as a "step backwards" not to include them.

According to recent reports, around 130 parties — among them vulnerable island nations, developing countries and richer EU members — called for the reintroduction of the two words into the text, to no avail. And so many refused to support the adoption of the final COP agreement.

Sources indicate that the deadlock signals a failure for the UN process. But the number of countries willing to walk away from what they saw as a weak text was, arguably, a show of strength, and one that had been long coming.

The phrase "fossil fuels" first appeared three years ago in the closing decision of COP28 in Dubai with the promise of "transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems, in just, orderly and equitable manner." But it has been omitted from every text since.

Yet this year's climate summit was the first to acknowledge that the world will breach the critical 1.5-degree Celsius (2.7-degree Fahrenheit) threshold that scientists mentioned would safeguard the world from the worst impacts of planetary heating.

And so, the pressure was on for progress; to turn pledges from previous years into concrete action. But that progress didn't come.

"We don't celebrate the deep divisions exposed or the lack of a political signal from COP31 capable of driving climate action in line with science, equity and the law," remarked Nikki Reisch, director of the climate and energy program at the Center for International Environmental Law.

"But the rejected text would have done more harm than good.".

The lack of agreement was not solely about fossil fuels; money also played a part.

Developing nations have long argued that they need additional financing, both as a means for them to move away from coal, oil and gas, but also to help them cope with the consequences of rising temperatures.

Recent findings suggest that countries all over the world are being battered by extreme weather events. Catastrophes like flooding, drought and wildfires have been fueled and worsened by rising global temperatures. Often the worst hit are poorer countries with low rates of greenhouse gas emissions.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that and yet, richer states behind much of the historical emissions are increasingly unwilling to foot the bill. Dissatisfaction at home due to higher food and fuel prices has left many governments loathe to pay more to finance climate action abroad.

With the United States  — the world's biggest historical emitter  — now absent from negotiations and on the verge of leaving the United Nation's Framework Convention on Climate Change, the European Union was portrayed as this year's villain with some observers accusing the EU of hypocrisy.

"You can't demand action and then block the finance that makes this possible," Fanny Petitbon, policy analyst at 350.org, mentioned in a statement.

As the world's largest provider of climate finance, the EU reportedly refused to negotiate on providing additional finance and has repeatedly called for other nations to step up.

The failure to find an agreement is a particularly bitter turn of events for countries that face ever worsening impacts of climate change, like the island states that are being confronted by a reality that could see their countries wiped off the map as sea levels rise.

Although the Turkey-led electrification agenda calling for an increase in global electricity consumption to 35% by 2035 was not formally adopted — it made up part of the rejected final agreement — more than 90 countries pledged to move forward regardless.

According to recent reports, it's not a silver bullet. There was no agreement on ensuring the increase was forged only through clean, renewable energy. But it would still signal forward momentum, driven by economic forces and a need for home-grown energy security.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

And there are other hopes. The second conference on the Just Transition Away from Fossil Fuels will take place in Tuvalu in July 2027. Initiated at the COP30 conference last year in Belem, Brazil, it has seen increasing support from countries putting together concrete roadmaps for abandoning coal, oil and gas.

There has been much talk of blame and who is responsible for the breakdown and collapse of talks. What is clear is that the UN climate summits need reform. Progress, when it does happen, is slow. The present model, based on consensus, requires all countries to agree on every measure. There have been many calls for majority-rule decision making, which might have forced the inclusion of language like "fossil fuels" into the text.

But ultimately, this is not the time to focus on fault. As the climate crisis accelerates, governments need to reflect — and swiftly — on what can be done outside of these UN processes, within their nations, to speed up climate action.

"The take-home message from COP31 is clear: the world must do much more to confront the climate crisis — and it must do it now," said UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres in a statement.
